events.name: RootedCON - Entrepreneurship Track
events.description: Impulsamos una colaboración de un año con RootedCon, una de las mayores comunidades de ciberseguridad de Europa, participando en sesiones por toda España y culminando en un evento estrella en Madrid con más de 9.000 asistentes. Aunque RootedCon está muy consolidado entre hackers y profesionales de ciberseguridad, sus sesiones históricamente no incluían nada sobre negocio, startups o venture capital. Gracias a Juan, Kibo Ventures diseñó e introdujo un track de emprendimiento, dando incluso a los asistentes más técnicos una base de negocio. 🔗 ***Enlaces***
events.description_en: Drove a year-long partnership with RootedCon, one of the largest cybersecurity communities in Europe, participating in sessions across Spain and culminating in a flagship event in Madrid that drew over 9,000 attendees. While RootedCon is well established among hackers and cybersecurity professionals, its sessions had historically included nothing on business, startups, or venture capital. Thanks to Juan, Kibo Ventures designed and introduced an entrepreneurship track, giving even the most technical attendees a foundational sense of business. 🔗 ***Links***

events.name: Inside the Black Box - AI Kibo Community
events.description: Inside the Black Box es una nueva serie de sesiones en la oficina de Kibo Ventures, con expertos en IA e industria para conversaciones abiertas sobre qué mueve realmente a las compañías más interesantes de hoy. Nació de AI Kibo Community, un grupo de WhatsApp donde founders del portfolio, expertos de sector y el equipo de Kibo comparten ideas sobre IA. La primera edición contó con Pedro Torrecillas, VP de Producto en Job&Talent, que compartió su visión sobre cómo la IA está transformando el talento y las operaciones.
events.description_en: Inside the Black Box is a new session series hosted at Kibo Ventures' office, where we bring in AI and industry experts for candid conversations on what's really driving today's most interesting companies. The series grew out of AI Kibo Community, a WhatsApp group where founders from our portfolio companies, sector experts, and members of the Kibo team gather to share ideas and discuss what's happening in AI. The first edition featured Pedro Torrecillas, VP of Product at Job&Talent, who shared his perspective on how AI is transforming talent and operations.

events.name: Anual Investor Meeting 2024
events.description: Como siempre, un día muy especial para el equipo de Kibo Ventures al recibir a nuestros inversores, founders y líderes de la industria de toda Europa en nuestro Annual Investor Meeting. Tuvimos la suerte de contar con un grupo fantástico de founders para ilustrar nuestra tesis de inversión. - *“Convirtiendo los riesgos climáticos globales en oportunidades de inversión”* con Alejandro Martí de Mitiga Solutions, Alejandro Cabrera de Green Eagle Solutions y Javier de la Torre de Carto. - *“Creación de valor en deep tech: construir en local y crecer en global”* con Pedro Castillo de Onum, Daniel Solís de Zynap, Chema Molina de Frenetic y Carlos Pardo de KD. - *“Inversión con propósito: usar la tecnología para abordar retos sociales”* con Oriol Fuertes de Qida y Bernat Portell de Innovamat.
events.description_en: As always very special day for the team at Kibo Ventures as we welcomed our investors, founders, and industry leaders from across Europe for our Annual Investor Meeting. Lucky to count with a fantastic group of founders to illustrate our investment thesis. - *“Turning global climate risks into investment opportunities”* with Alejandro Martí from Mitiga Solutions, Alejandro Cabrera from Green Eagle Solutions, and Javier de la Torre from Carto. - *“Value creation in deep tech: build local and grow global”* with Pedro Castillo from Onum, Daniel Solis from Zynap, Chema Molina from Frenetic, and Carlos Pardo from KD. - *“Purpose-driven investment: Leveraging tech to address societal challenges”* with Oriol Fuertes from Qida and Bernat Portell from Innovamat.

events.name: Roundtables with Edmond de Rothschild
events.description: Evento co-organizado con Edmond de Rothschild, reuniendo a founders de éxito, inversores y expertos de la industria. El objetivo era construir relaciones valiosas entre nuestros emprendedores de éxito y expertos en banca privada. Además, el evento profundizó en la importancia para los founders de contar con un buen socio fiscal y financiero. La agenda incluyó dos mesas redondas: 💻 *Mesa 1*: *“Ventajas y retos de invertir en tecnología”* - Rodrigo Cebrián y Maguy MacDonald (Edmond de Rothschild), Juan Santamaría (HWK) y Javier Torremocha (Kibo Ventures) compartieron perspectivas sobre las complejidades y grandes oportunidades de invertir en tecnología. 🤝 *Mesa 2*: *“Cómo gestionar un evento de liquidez”* - Olivier Tremeaud (Edmond de Rothschild), Eduardo Cruz (Qustodio y Redtrust), Javier Povo (Pérez-Llorca) y Juan López (Kibo Ventures) hablaron sobre las claves para planificar eventos de liquidez, sin olvidar las dificultades emocionales y financieras, a menudo olvidadas, de planificar el futuro tras un exit.
events.description_en: Co-hosted event with Edmond de Rothschild, bringing together successful founders, investors, and industry experts. The objective was to build valuable relations between our succesful entrepreneurs with private banking experts. Furthermore, the event dove deep into the importance for founders of having a strong fiscal and financial parter. The agenda featured two roundtables: 💻 *Roundtable 1*: *“Advantages and Challenges of Investing in Tech”* - Rodrigo Cebrián and Maguy MacDonald (Edmond de Rothschild), Juan Santamaría (HWK), and Javier Torremocha (Kibo Ventures) shared perspectives on the complexities and large opportunities of tech investing. 🤝 *Roundtable 2*: *“How to Manage a Liquidity Event”* - Olivier Tremeaud (Edmond de Rothschild), Eduardo Cruz (Qustodio and Redtrust), Javier Povo (Pérez-Llorca), and Juan Lopez (Kibo Ventures) discussed key considerations in planning liquidity events whilst thinking of the often forgotten emotional and financial difficulties of planning the future after an exit.

Esta liga reúne a protagonistas del ecosistema tecnológico e innovador que tienen la oportunidad de conectar y conocerse de forma informal, siendo una excelente oportunidad de networking. Las siguientes empresas participan en la liga: Paypal, PandaGo, Santander, Trucksters, Telefónica, Revolut, Automat-IT, Clevergy, Gibobs, Endeavor, Toqio, Heytrade, Bdeo, Odilo, Snab, Ucademy.
events.description_en: Our paddle league designed to connect members of the entrepreneurial ecosystem while we enjoy practicing an exciting sport like paddle, which enhances teamwork, strategy and commitment to a common goal. knowledge_chunks.content: At Kibo, we firmly believe that entrepreneurship isn't about being unconventional; it's about showcasing exceptional courage. We do our homework and research their market fit, readiness to scale, social and environmental impact before we add them to our portfolios. Once in, things move fast, and if they don't, we stick with our founders for the long haul.

knowledge_chunks.section: Vision, mission and how we work
knowledge_chunks.content: Vision & Mission: To fund and support outstanding founders who bring positive solutions to humanity's biggest challenges through technology, while generating top quartile returns for our investors. We are team players, patient capital, supporting partners (we do not manage companies), co-investor friendly, humble and grounded, with a long-term relationship view.

knowledge_chunks.source_page: How to do first-class board meetings
knowledge_chunks.section: Best practices before and during the meeting
knowledge_chunks.content: Take a step back and look at your company strategically. Focus on the 'so what' of the data you present. Ask the board for explicit help. Share documents 48 hours beforehand. Keep track of action items. Collect feedback after every meeting.

knowledge_chunks.source_page: How to do first-class board meetings
knowledge_chunks.content: The board deck covers: Agenda with time per section, Highlights of the quarter (achievements/challenges), Main KPIs vs budget with status, Financials (P&L and Balance Sheet), a KPI evolution chart, Product updates, Organizational structure and hiring needs, Deep dives (>50% of meeting time), and Housekeeping (approvals, comp committee, ESOP).

knowledge_chunks.source_page: Your Guide to a Winning Deck (Series A/B)
knowledge_chunks.content: 1. Cover/Company name in a single sentence. 2. Problem: who suffers it, how it's solved today, why it's urgent. 3. Solution: core benefits, is it 10x better. 4. Product: functionalities and unfair advantage. 5. Market: TAM/SAM/SOM bottom-up. 6. Competition: honest comparison matrix. 7. Why now. 8. Traction/financials: MRR growth drivers, retention cohorts. 9. Business model & unit economics: GMV, net revenue, gross margin. 10. Team: composition, track record, founder-problem fit. 11. The round: amount, use of funds, past investors. 12. Closing/contact.

knowledge_chunks.source_page: How to nail your new round
knowledge_chunks.section: Pitch deck, business plan and data room checklists
knowledge_chunks.content: Pitch deck order: Vision, Problem, Solution/Product, Business Model, Market Size, KPIs & Financials, Team, Competition, Roadmap, Deal structure. Business plan: Historicals, main KPIs, bottom-up growth assumptions, future projection, P&L/BS/CF summary, sanity checks. Data room: company summary, cap table, convertible notes, shareholder agreements, financials & traction, growth plan, market analysis, team & org, legal docs.

knowledge_chunks.source_page: How to nail your Series A (Aquilino Peña presentation)
knowledge_chunks.section: Is your business VC-backable and what Series A-ready looks like
knowledge_chunks.content: Ask if your business is VC-backable before raising: VC funds need huge outcomes. A Series A-ready company has: an international, ambitious, execution-proven team of 2-4 founders; product-market fit and 10x-better product; a fast-growing, not-saturated market; proven unit economics and 18-24 months runway; founders owning >60%, ESOP in place, sensible governance.

knowledge_chunks.source_page: How to nail your Series A (Aquilino Peña presentation)
knowledge_chunks.section: How to run the fundraising process
knowledge_chunks.content: Build a monthly investor update. Get warm intros from current investors, other founders, or later-stage investors. Study each fund's strategy before reaching out; aim for Partners but treat Associates/Principals as allies. Track funds by geo focus, ticket size, stage, and status (intro done, pitch sent, Q&A, partners sheet) kanban-style.

knowledge_chunks.source_page: How can I improve my reporting skills
knowledge_chunks.content: Structure: Financial metrics (cash, burn, runway, revenue/MRR, EBITDA vs forecast). Core business metrics (company North Stars vs forecast). Highlights. Lowlights and how they're being solved. Product updates. What's on our mind. Other updates. Help needed. Companies who report best, perform best.

Llama-Berry - Improved Mathematical Reasoning
ai_repository.notes: Resumen: este paper presenta un framework avanzado de resolución de problemas matemáticos, LLaMA-Berry, para mejorar la capacidad de razonamiento matemático de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLMs). El framework combina Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) con Self-Refine iterativo para optimizar el camino de razonamiento y utiliza un modelo de recompensa por pares para evaluar distintos caminos de forma global. Aprovechando las capacidades de autocrítica y reescritura de los LLMs, Self-Refine aplicado a MCTS (SR-MCTS) supera las ineficiencias y limitaciones de los algoritmos de búsqueda voraz tradicionales, favoreciendo una exploración más eficiente del espacio de soluciones. El Pairwise Preference Reward Model (PPRM), inspirado en el Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), se usa después para modelar preferencias entre pares de soluciones, utilizando un método de Enhanced Borda Count (EBC) para sintetizar esas preferencias en una puntuación de ranking global y encontrar mejores respuestas. Este enfoque aborda los retos de la variabilidad en las puntuaciones y las distribuciones no independientes en tareas de razonamiento matemático. El framework se ha probado en benchmarks generales y avanzados, mostrando un rendimiento superior en eficiencia de búsqueda y capacidad de resolución de problemas frente a métodos existentes como ToT y rStar, especialmente en benchmarks complejos de nivel olimpiada, incluyendo GPQA, AIME24 y AMC23.
ai_repository.notes_en: Abstract: This paper presents an advanced mathematical problem-solving framework, LLaMA-Berry, for enhancing the mathematical reasoning ability of Large Language Models (LLMs). The framework combines Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with iterative Self-Refine to optimize the reasoning path and utilizes a pairwise reward model to evaluate different paths globally. By leveraging the self-critic and rewriting capabilities of LLMs, Self-Refine applied to MCTS (SR-MCTS) overcomes the inefficiencies and limitations of conventional step-wise and greedy search algorithms by fostering a more efficient exploration of solution spaces. Pairwise Preference Reward Model (PPRM), inspired by Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), is then used to model pairwise preferences between solutions, utilizing an Enhanced Borda Count (EBC) method to synthesize these preferences into a global ranking score to find better answers. This approach addresses the challenges of scoring variability and non-independent distributions in mathematical reasoning tasks. The framework has been tested on general and advanced benchmarks, showing superior performance in terms of search efficiency and problem-solving capability compared to existing methods like ToT and rStar, particularly in complex Olympiad-level benchmarks, including GPQA, AIME24, and AMC23.

ai_repository.title: LLMs and Law Application
ai_repository.notes: Resumen: este paper analiza si los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLMs) pueden aplicar la ley. No cuestiona si los LLMs deberían aplicar la ley, sino que distingue entre dos interpretaciones de la pregunta “pueden”. Primero, ¿pueden los LLMs aplicar la ley como individuos ordinarios? Segundo, ¿pueden aplicarla del mismo modo que los jueces? El estudio examina la teoría de aplicación del derecho de D'Almeida, dividida en aplicación inferencial y pragmática. Argumenta que su planteamiento de la aplicación pragmática puede mejorarse, ya que no tiene en cuenta plenamente que la aplicación del derecho (y el seguimiento de reglas) es una práctica pública y compartida, realizada colectivamente por los miembros de una comunidad lingüística. El estudio concluye que los LLMs no pueden aplicar la ley: no pueden hacerlo en el sentido inferencial, ya que solo tienen una interacción sintáctica (no semántica) con la ley, y tampoco en el sentido pragmático, puesto que la aplicación pragmática del derecho no depende de un único agente, sea este un juez, un ciudadano ordinario o una entidad no humana.
ai_repository.notes_en: Abstract: This paper asks whether large language models (LLMs) can apply the law. It does not question whether LLMs should apply the law. Instead, it distinguishes between two interpretations of the 'can' question. One, can LLMs apply the law like ordinary individuals? Two, can LLMs apply the law in the same manner as judges? The study examines D'Almeida's theory of law application, divided into inferential and pragmatic law application. It argues that his account of pragmatic law application can be improved as it does not fully consider that law application (and rule-following) is a shared, public practice collectively realized by members of a linguistic community. The study concludes that LLMs cannot apply the law: they cannot apply it in the inferential sense as they have mere syntactic (not semantic) interaction with the law, and they cannot apply it in the pragmatic sense since pragmatic law application does not depend on a single agent, whether that agent is a judge, an ordinary citizen, or a non-human entity.

Sam Altman at YC: How to build the future
ai_repository.notes: Entrevista de Sam Altman: Cómo construir el futuro - Notas sobre IA. Hace tiempo que no vivíamos una revolución tecnológica como la de la IA; Sam cree que este es el mejor momento de la historia para construir una empresa tecnológica. El principal cuello de botella para la AGI en la próxima década es la energía: cree que la solar es suficiente por ahora, pero un avance en energía nuclear aceleraría el desarrollo de la AGI. Es optimista con las startups porque la mayoría de las grandes tecnológicas no están viendo lo que está pasando en IA. Define el camino hacia la AGI en cinco niveles: (1) Chatbots, (2) Razonamiento (como ChatGPT), (3) Agentes (capaces de completar tareas e interactuar con su entorno — dice que o1 ya puede hacerlo), (4) Innovadores (capaces de explorar fenómenos poco comprendidos), y (5) todo lo anterior a escala. Está entusiasmado con los avances en AGI de 2025. Aprendizajes de los primeros días en OpenAI: tener una visión clara es esencial en las primeras etapas — Sam convenció a Ilya y a otros de sumarse persiguiendo la AGI cuando ese objetivo parecía absurdo, lo que atrajo a gente con talento (aunque algo temeraria) y alejó a los mediocres; muchos líderes destacados predijeron un largo invierno de la IA, pero el equipo confió en los datos a medida que los resultados mejoraban; eligieron un único foco y se dedicaron a él por completo. Reflexiones sobre construir startups: la convicción extrema en una idea concreta es el rasgo más poderoso de una startup; el talento y rodearte de gente inteligente y trabajadora importa muchísimo — tardaron nueve meses en montar el equipo inicial de OpenAI. Consejos para founders ahora: apostar por la tendencia de la IA, ya que los modelos van a mejorar rápidamente — la velocidad, el foco y la convicción son una ventaja poderosa; buscar una explosión de crecimiento a corto plazo adoptando tecnología como la IA más rápido que otros, mientras se construye algo con valor duradero.
ai_repository.notes_en: Sam Altman's interview: How To Build The Future - Notes About AI. It's been a while since we've had a tech revolution like AI; Sam believes this is the best time ever to build a tech company. The main bottleneck for AGI in the next decade is energy — he believes solar is sufficient for now, but a breakthrough in nuclear energy would accelerate AGI development. He's bullish on startups because most tech incumbents are overlooking what's happening in AI. He defines the path to AGI in five levels: (1) Chatbots, (2) Reasoning (like ChatGPT), (3) Agents (capable of completing tasks and interacting with their environment — claims o1 can do it), (4) Innovators (able to explore poorly understood phenomena), and (5) all of the previous at scale. He's excited about AGI developments in 2025. Learnings from the early days at OpenAI: having a clear vision is essential — Sam convinced Ilya and others to join him by pursuing AGI when that goal seemed absurd, which attracted talented (if reckless) people while deterring mediocre ones; many prominent leaders predicted a prolonged AI winter, but the team trusted the data as results kept improving; they chose a single focus and dedicated themselves to it. Insights on building startups: extreme conviction in one specific idea is the most powerful trait of a startup; talent and surrounding yourself with hard-working, intelligent people matters enormously — it took nine months to assemble the initial OpenAI team. Advice for founders now: bet on the AI trend since models are set to improve rapidly — speed, focus and conviction are a powerful advantage; aim for a short-term explosion of growth by adopting new tech like AI faster than others, while building something with enduring value.
